subject: physics
title: Circular Motion & Gravitation Adventure 3: Gravitational potential and energy
welcome_lead: Today you'll define gravitational potential and escape Earth.
meta_desc: Physics HL — gravitational potential V = -GM/r, potential energy = -GMm/r, escape velocity.
final_note: You learned V = -GM/r (taking ∞ as zero); PE = -GMm/r; escape v = √(2GM/r); total orbital energy is negative.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Gravitational potential at distance r from M:

V = -GM/r (J/kg)

Negative because attractive — would do positive work moving toward M.

Reference: V = 0 at infinity.

PE = mV = -GMm/r

For circular orbit: ½mv² = GMm/(2r), and PE = -GMm/r.

Total: E_total = ½mv² + PE = -GMm/(2r)

Negative → bound orbit. Higher orbit = less negative = more total energy.

To escape (reach infinity with v=0):

½mv² + (-GMm/r) = 0
v_escape = √(2GM/r)

Earth: ~11.2 km/s. Sun: ~617 km/s.

Black hole: at Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c², v_esc = c → light trapped.

mcqs.q: Gravitational potential of Earth at infinity:
Does light always travel at the same speed?
options: No — light always slows with distance from its source.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
Yes — c is a universal constant in every situation.
Only in a vacuum; in any material medium (water, glass) light travels more slowly, which is what causes refraction.

mcqs.q: What absorber is needed to stop beta radiation?
options: A few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
A sheet of paper — beta is only slightly more penetrating than alpha.

mcqs.q: If one EM wave has a higher frequency than another, what is true about its wavelength?
options: It is unchanged — only the speed differs.
It is also longer, because both increase together.
It is shorter — wavelength and frequency are inversely related (c = f x lambda).
No — light always slows with distance from its source.
